The finite obstructions are single-edge cuts and short stable cycles as in the descent analysis, but the key asymmetry is BASIN, not count: for every static obstruction present (Poisson many, constant expected count) the basin is large, and more importantly the descent dynamics on a random initial coloring with \u0398(n) crossing edges has, with probability \u2192 1, a positive-density chance per realization of locking before global consensus because the cut-descent flow is trapped by ANY local minimum created en route \u2014 and the number of local minima reachable from a random start is \u0398(n) with per-minimum basins of total measure \u2192 1. Equivalently: the final state is a local minimum of a random landscape with exponentially many local minima, and the global minimum occupies vanishing basin fraction.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A coupling/monotonicity argument showing the descent reaches the global minimum whp from a random start (e.g., via coalescing of monochromatic regions)","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Simulation evidence that consensus probability stays bounded away from 0 for large n","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Proof that reachable local minima are only the Poisson-count static obstructions, with total basin \u2192 0","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Majority updating is a strict Lyapunov descent on crossing-edge count; every asynchronous run terminates at a local minimum of the cut. Local minima of the cut landscape on a 3-regular random graph are dense: for any maximal matching M of size \u03b1n, the coloring with monochromatic G\u2212M components is locally stable (SRC_011's construction), and exponentially many such colorings exist. A random initial coloring, under a greedy descent, is equivalent to a zero-temperature quench of a 3-spin majority system \u2014 the archetypal scenario for residual entropy: the fraction of descents reaching the global minimum in such quenches decays exponentially in system size because each of the \u0398(n) independent regions must all, simultaneously, flow to agreement, and each region has constant probability of locally locking into an incompatible orientation. By locality (the update is 1-neighborhood), the process decomposes over the graph's expansion: disagreements on \u0398(n) well-separated length-2 paths freeze independently, giving P(consensus) \u2264 (1-p)^{\u0398(n)} = exp(-\u0398(n)) \u2192 0.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
